metadata.title: Implement Loading State with User Feedback

story.iWant: clear feedback while my request is processing
story.soThat: I know the app is working on my answer
story.tasks:
- Task 1: Create LoadingState component (AC: 1) - Create new file `components/LoadingState.tsx` - Add loading spinner or animation (use Shadcn UI Spinner if available, or custom) - Add "Checking forecast..." text message - Add ARIA live region for screen reader announcements - Export component with optional message prop - Style component to match landing page design
- Task 2: Implement ARIA live region for accessibility (AC: 1) - Add aria-live="polite" attribute to loading container - Add role="status" for screen reader announcement - Ensure message is announced when loading state appears - Test with screen reader (VoiceOver or NVDA) if available - Verify announcement doesn't interrupt user actions
- Task 3: Integrate LoadingState into page.tsx (AC: 1) - Import LoadingState component into `app/page.tsx` - Add conditional rendering based on isLoading state - Position loading indicator appropriately (below button, centered) - Replace button text loading indicator with LoadingState component - Ensure loading appears immediately on form submission (<100ms) - Verify loading disappears when API response received
- Task 4: Style loading indicator for visual consistency (AC: 1) - Use Tailwind CSS utilities for styling - Center loading indicator in layout - Add appropriate spacing (margin-top from button) - Ensure loading indicator is visible on all backgrounds - Make loading indicator responsive (works on mobile/tablet/desktop) - Use consistent color palette with rest of application
- Task 5: Test loading state timing and behavior (AC: 1) - Verify loading appears within 100ms of form submission - Verify loading persists during API call (typical <2 seconds) - Verify loading disappears on successful API response - Verify loading disappears on error API response - Test with network throttling (Fast 3G) to see longer loading - Ensure no visual flicker or layout shift
- Task 6: Manual testing and validation (AC: 1) - Test loading state with valid location search - Test loading state with invalid location (error scenario) - Test keyboard accessibility (screen reader announcements) - Verify input and button remain disabled during loading - Test on mobile, tablet, and desktop viewports - TypeScript compilation passes (npm run type-check) - ESLint validation passes (npm run lint) - Verify no console errors in browser

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
AC-1: Loading State Provides Immediate Feedback
**Given** a location search is submitted **When** the API request is in progress **Then** a loading indicator is displayed **And** the input field is disabled to prevent duplicate requests **And** loading state is announced to screen readers **And** loading completes within expected timeframe (<2 seconds typical) **And** loading indicator disappears when result arrives **And** loading indicator disappears if error occurs

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: LoadingState component: Presentational component with props interface { message?: string }, uses aria-live="polite" and role="status" for screen reader announcements, conditionally rendered when isLoading state is true. Options include Shadcn UI Spinner, custom CSS spinner, or simple animated ellipsis text.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: Accessibility Requirements: ARIA live regions with aria-live="polite" for loading states announces loading without interrupting user, role="status" identifies as status message for screen readers. Loading state announced when becomes visible.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: Performance target: Loading indicator appears within 100ms of form submission. React renders LoadingState immediately when isLoading changes. No artificial loading delays. Reserve space for loading indicator to avoid content jump.

doc.title: Epic Technical Specification: Simple Answer Experience
doc.snippet: Testing Approach for Epic 3: Manual browser testing on localhost:3000, no automated unit tests (deferred to Epic 5), TypeScript compilation validation, ESLint validation, keyboard accessibility testing, cross-browser testing deferred to Epic 4.7. Primary browser: Chrome.

doc.title: Epic Breakdown
doc.section: Story 3.3: Implement Loading State with User Feedback
doc.snippet: As a user, I want clear feedback while my request is processing, So that I know the app is working on my answer. Prerequisites: Story 3.2 (location input). Technical notes: Use Shadcn UI Spinner or custom loading component, manage loading state in React, add aria-live region for screen reader announcements, implement timeout handling, show loading immediately on submission, clear loading state on success or error.

doc.title: Story 3.2: Create Location Input Field with Validation
doc.snippet: Loading state management already implemented: isLoading state variable exists with useState, loading lifecycle implemented (set to true on submit, set to false in finally block after API response), input and button already disabled during loading with disabled={isLoading}, button text already changes to "Checking..." during loading. Story 3.3 adds visual loading component.

file.reason: Main landing page component that manages isLoading state (line 46), handles form submission and API calls (lines 66-110), already disables input and button during loading (lines 139, 155). Story 3.3 adds LoadingState component rendering conditional on isLoading state.

Boolean state variable already implemented: const [isLoading, setIsLoading] = useState(false). Set to true on form submit (line 77), set to false in finally block (line 107). LoadingState component will render conditionally based on this state.

Form submission handler that manages loading lifecycle: validates input, sets isLoading=true (line 77), calls API, handles response, sets isLoading=false in finally block (line 107). LoadingState component will display during the isLoading=true window.
Shadcn UI Input component already used in page.tsx (line 127). Disabled during loading with disabled={isLoading} prop. Provides reference for styling pattern and disabled state.

Shadcn UI Button component already used in page.tsx (line 153). Disabled during loading with disabled={isLoading} prop. Shows loading text "Checking..." (line 158). LoadingState component will provide visual loading indicator below button.

dependency.reason: Optional: Icon library if using icon-based spinner

constraint.description: LoadingState must be a presentational component (not container component). Receives props, renders UI only. No state management inside LoadingState.
LoadingState props interface: { message?: string } with default "Checking forecast...". Optional message prop allows customization while providing sensible default.
ARIA live region required: aria-live="polite" for non-interruptive announcements, role="status" for status message identification. Screen reader must announce loading state when it appears.
LoadingState only renders when isLoading state is true in parent component (page.tsx). Conditional rendering pattern: {isLoading && <LoadingState />}

Use Tailwind CSS utilities exclusively for styling. No custom CSS files. Follow mobile-first responsive design pattern. Ensure loading indicator centers correctly at all breakpoints (320px, 768px, 1024px).

Loading indicator must appear within 100ms of form submission. React renders immediately when isLoading changes - no artificial delays (setTimeout). Avoid layout shift by reserving space for loading indicator.

Three implementation options: (1) Use Shadcn UI Spinner component if available, (2) Create custom CSS spinner using Tailwind utilities, (3) Use simple animated ellipsis text. Recommendation: Start with simple spinner + text, defer complex animations to Epic 5.
Create new file at will-it-rain/components/LoadingState.tsx. Modify existing file will-it-rain/app/page.tsx to import and render LoadingState. Follow project structure conventions.
All imports use absolute path aliases with @ prefix. Import pattern: import { LoadingState } from '@/components/LoadingState'. Follows existing project convention from Stories 3.1 and 3.2.

No new state management needed. Reuse existing isLoading state variable from page.tsx (line 46). Loading lifecycle already implemented: setIsLoading(true) on submit (line 77), setIsLoading(false) in finally block (line 107).

Button text currently changes to "Checking..." during loading (line 158 in page.tsx). Can keep this or remove it after adding LoadingState component. Priority: Ensure ARIA announcement and visual indicator both work.

Testing approach: Manual browser testing on localhost:3000, TypeScript compilation validation (npm run type-check), ESLint validation (npm run lint), keyboard accessibility testing. No automated unit tests (deferred to Epic 5). Test with network throttling (Fast 3G) to observe loading state.

tests.standards: Epic 3 uses manual browser testing with TypeScript and ESLint validation. No automated unit tests (deferred to Epic 5.7). Testing standards: (1) Manual testing on localhost:3000 during development, (2) TypeScript compilation with npm run type-check, (3) ESLint validation with npm run lint, (4) Keyboard accessibility testing (Tab navigation, screen reader if available), (5) Cross-browser testing deferred to Epic 4.7 (develop in Chrome), (6) Responsive design testing on mobile/tablet/desktop viewports.
tests.locations: will-it-rain/app/page.tsx (no test files yet - manual testing only) Testing approach: Start dev server (npm run dev), open localhost:3000, submit form, observe loading state appearance/disappearance

test.description: Verify loading indicator appears within 100ms of form submission
test.approach: Submit form with valid location (e.g., "San Francisco" or "94102"), observe loading indicator appears immediately, use browser DevTools Performance tab to measure timing if needed
test.expected: Loading indicator (spinner + "Checking forecast..." text) appears within 100ms, positioned below button, centered in layout

test.description: Verify loading indicator disappears when API returns success response
test.approach: Submit form with valid location, wait for API response (typically <2 seconds), observe loading indicator disappears when answer displays
test.expected: Loading indicator disappears, answer or error display appears in its place (Stories 3.4/3.5/3.7 will implement display)

test.description: Verify loading indicator disappears when API returns error response
test.approach: Submit form with invalid location (e.g., "XYZ123"), wait for API response, observe loading indicator disappears when error displays
test.expected: Loading indicator disappears, error display appears (Story 3.7 will implement error display)

test.description: Verify screen reader announces loading state
test.approach: Enable VoiceOver (macOS: Cmd+F5) or NVDA (Windows), submit form with location, listen for "Checking forecast..." announcement
test.expected: Screen reader announces loading message when LoadingState appears, aria-live="polite" ensures non-interruptive announcement

test.description: Verify loading indicator is visible and centered on all viewports
test.approach: Open browser DevTools, set responsive mode, test at 320px (mobile), 768px (tablet), 1024px (desktop), submit form, observe loading indicator centering and visibility
test.expected: Loading indicator centers correctly at all breakpoints, text is readable, spinner is visible, spacing is appropriate

test.description: Verify loading appearance doesn't cause layout shift or content jump
test.approach: Submit form, observe page layout before/during/after loading state, check if other elements move or shift position
test.expected: Loading indicator appears without causing layout shift, surrounding content remains stable, no visual flicker

test.description: Verify TypeScript compilation passes with zero errors
test.approach: Run npm run type-check in terminal, review output
test.expected: TypeScript compilation succeeds with no errors, LoadingState component props interface is correctly typed

test.description: Verify ESLint validation passes with zero errors
test.approach: Run npm run lint in terminal, review output
test.expected: ESLint validation passes with no errors or warnings, code follows Next.js and TypeScript linting rules

test.description: Test loading state persistence with network throttling to simulate slower connection
test.approach: Open browser DevTools, go to Network tab, set throttling to "Fast 3G", submit form with location, observe loading state persists longer
test.expected: Loading state remains visible for full duration of API call (may be 3-5 seconds with throttling), disappears when response received

test.description: Verify input and button remain disabled during loading to prevent duplicate requests
test.approach: Submit form, while loading indicator is visible, attempt to type in input field and click button again
test.expected: Input field is disabled (grayed out, not accepting input), button is disabled (grayed out, not clickable), prevents duplicate API requests
